quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [Data Privacy Concerns] Many smartphone apps request access to a user's contacts, location, and camera even when those features are not directly needed for the app to function. Privacy researchers argue that this practice, often buried in lengthy terms of service that few people read, allows companies to collect far more personal data than most users realize. As awareness grows, some regulators are now requiring apps to explain, in plain language, exactly why each permission is needed.
quests.question: Why does the passage suggest many users don't realize how much data is collected?
options: The details are buried in terms of service few people read
Apps do not legally have to disclose anything
Most apps do not request any permissions
Regulators have banned all data collection
quests.correctAnswer: The details are buried in terms of service few people read
quests.hint: Look at what the passage says about where this information is hidden.
quests.explanation: The passage explains that the practice is often buried in lengthy terms of service that few people read, which is why users are often unaware.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [Mental Health Awareness at Work] More companies are training managers to recognize early signs of burnout, such as declining performance, withdrawal from colleagues, or unusual irritability. Rather than waiting for an employee to reach a crisis point, these programs encourage managers to check in privately and point staff toward available support resources. Advocates say this shift represents a move from reacting to problems toward preventing them in the first place.
quests.question: What shift do advocates say these training programs represent?
options: A move from private support to public discussion
A move from reacting to problems to preventing them
A move away from manager involvement entirely
A move toward stricter performance reviews
quests.correctAnswer: A move from reacting to problems to preventing them
quests.hint: The shift being described is summarized in the last sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says advocates view the training as shifting the focus from reacting to burnout toward preventing it.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [Negotiating Salary] Career coaches often advise job candidates to avoid naming a specific salary figure first, since whoever speaks first tends to set the boundaries for the entire negotiation. Instead, they suggest turning the question back to the employer by asking about the budgeted range for the role. This small shift, coaches claim, can prevent candidates from unintentionally asking for less than a company was actually prepared to offer.
quests.question: Why do coaches suggest asking the employer for a salary range first?
options: It guarantees a higher final salary
It is required during formal interviews
It shows the candidate lacks confidence
It can prevent candidates from asking for less than offered
quests.correctAnswer: It can prevent candidates from asking for less than offered
quests.hint: The benefit of this strategy is explained in the last sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage explains that asking first can prevent candidates from unintentionally requesting less than the company would have offered.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [Sustainable Tourism] As popular destinations struggle with overcrowding, some travel companies now promote 'slow travel,' encouraging visitors to spend more time in fewer places rather than rushing between famous landmarks. Proponents argue this approach not only reduces strain on fragile local infrastructure but also gives travelers a deeper, more meaningful understanding of the places they visit.
quests.question: What do proponents of slow travel claim it offers travelers?
options: A cheaper way to see more countries
A faster way to visit famous landmarks
A deeper, more meaningful understanding of places
A guaranteed discount on flights
quests.correctAnswer: A deeper, more meaningful understanding of places
quests.hint: The claimed benefit for travelers is in the last part of the passage.
quests.explanation: The passage says proponents believe slow travel gives visitors a deeper, more meaningful understanding of the places they visit.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [The Renewable Energy Transition] Grid operators face a unique challenge as more regions rely on solar and wind power: unlike traditional power plants, these sources cannot simply be switched on when demand rises, since their output depends on weather conditions. To manage this unpredictability, many utilities are now investing heavily in large battery systems that store excess energy for use when generation drops.
quests.question: Why are utilities investing in large battery systems?
options: To replace solar and wind power entirely
To store excess energy for when generation drops
To reduce the total cost of electricity
To eliminate the need for power grids
quests.correctAnswer: To store excess energy for when generation drops
quests.hint: The purpose of the batteries is explained in the last sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says the batteries store excess energy so it can be used when solar and wind generation drops.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [Critical Thinking Skills] Rather than simply memorizing facts, students in the new curriculum are taught to evaluate the reliability of a source before accepting its claims. Teachers present two conflicting articles on the same topic and ask students to identify potential bias, missing evidence, or unsupported assumptions in each. Supporters believe this method better prepares students for a world filled with competing, and sometimes misleading, information.
quests.question: What are students asked to do with the two conflicting articles?
options: Memorize both articles word for word
Identify potential bias, missing evidence, or unsupported assumptions
Choose which article is completely true
Rewrite the articles in their own words
quests.correctAnswer: Identify potential bias, missing evidence, or unsupported assumptions
quests.hint: The specific task is described in the second sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says students must identify bias, missing evidence, or unsupported assumptions in each article.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [A Streaming Algorithm] When a streaming service noticed that many viewers abandoned shows after the first episode, its data team discovered that recommendations based purely on genre were often misleading viewers' expectations. After adjusting the algorithm to weigh tone and pacing more heavily, the company reported a measurable increase in how many viewers finished an entire season.
quests.question: What problem did the data team discover with genre-based recommendations?
options: They were too slow to update
They only worked for new shows
They ignored viewer ratings completely
They often misled viewers' expectations
quests.correctAnswer: They often misled viewers' expectations
quests.hint: The problem is explained in the middle of the passage.
quests.explanation: The passage says genre-based recommendations often misled viewers about what a show would actually be like.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [Affordable Housing Initiative] To address a shortage of affordable homes, the city now requires that any new apartment building with more than twenty units set aside at least fifteen percent of those units for lower-income residents. Developers who comply receive tax reductions, while those who choose not to must pay into a separate housing fund instead.
quests.question: What happens to developers who do not set aside affordable units?
options: They are banned from future projects
They receive a larger tax reduction
They must pay into a separate housing fund
They must reduce the building's size
quests.correctAnswer: They must pay into a separate housing fund
quests.hint: The alternative for non-compliant developers is stated in the last sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says developers who do not comply must pay into a separate housing fund instead.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [Long-Distance Relationships] Researchers studying long-distance relationships found that couples who scheduled regular video calls, rather than calling only when something notable happened, reported feeling more emotionally connected over time. The consistency of contact, rather than its length, appeared to matter most for maintaining a sense of closeness.
quests.question: What mattered most for maintaining closeness, according to the research?
options: The consistency of contact
The length of each call
The number of gifts exchanged
The number of in-person visits
quests.correctAnswer: The consistency of contact
quests.hint: The key factor is stated in the last sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says consistency of contact, rather than length, mattered most for emotional closeness.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [A Fermentation Trend] Home fermentation, once considered a niche hobby, has grown rapidly in popularity as more people experiment with making their own yogurt, kimchi, and sourdough bread. Enthusiasts often cite the lower cost and the satisfaction of understanding exactly what goes into their food, though food safety experts caution that proper technique is essential to avoid harmful bacteria.
quests.question: What caution do food safety experts give about home fermentation?
options: It should only be done in restaurants
It is more expensive than buying food
Proper technique is essential to avoid harmful bacteria
It requires special government permission
quests.correctAnswer: Proper technique is essential to avoid harmful bacteria
quests.hint: The experts' warning appears at the end of the passage.
quests.explanation: The passage says experts caution that proper technique is essential to avoid harmful bacteria.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [Light Pollution] Astronomers have long warned that excessive outdoor lighting in cities makes it increasingly difficult to see stars, but recent studies suggest light pollution also disrupts the behavior of nocturnal animals, from disoriented sea turtle hatchlings to birds that migrate off course. In response, some cities have begun installing streetlights that dim automatically after midnight.
quests.question: How have some cities responded to concerns about light pollution?
options: By installing streetlights that dim after midnight
By banning all outdoor lighting
By moving city centers away from coastlines
By relocating affected wildlife
quests.correctAnswer: By installing streetlights that dim after midnight
quests.hint: The cities' response is described in the last sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says some cities now install streetlights that dim automatically after midnight.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [Blending Immigrant Traditions] When Mrs. Oyelaran immigrated decades ago, she began adapting her family's traditional recipes to include ingredients that were easier to find locally, without abandoning the dishes' original spirit. Her grandchildren now consider these adapted versions to be the 'authentic' family recipes, unaware that they differ from what was originally cooked back home.
quests.question: What do Mrs. Oyelaran's grandchildren believe about the adapted recipes?
options: They know the recipes have changed significantly
They prefer the original, unadapted dishes
They refuse to eat the adapted versions
They believe the adapted versions are the authentic family recipes
quests.correctAnswer: They believe the adapted versions are the authentic family recipes
quests.hint: The grandchildren's belief is described in the last sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says the grandchildren consider the adapted recipes authentic, not realizing they differ from the originals.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [Workplace Open-Plan Debate] Open-plan offices were originally introduced to encourage spontaneous collaboration between employees, but several recent studies have found the opposite effect: workers in open layouts often send more messages and have less face-to-face conversation than those in private offices, possibly due to a desire for auditory privacy.
quests.question: What unexpected result have recent studies found about open-plan offices?
options: Workers are more productive than before
Workers prefer open offices overall
Workers take more breaks than before
Workers have less face-to-face conversation than expected
quests.correctAnswer: Workers have less face-to-face conversation than expected
quests.hint: The unexpected finding is described in the middle of the passage.
quests.explanation: The passage says studies found workers in open offices have less face-to-face conversation, the opposite of the original goal.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [A Community Repair Café] At the monthly repair café, volunteers with backgrounds in electronics and sewing help neighbors fix broken appliances and torn clothing for free rather than throwing them away. Organizers say the event has repaired more than a thousand items since it started, keeping a significant amount of waste out of local landfills.
quests.question: What is the main purpose of the repair café?
options: To help neighbors fix items instead of throwing them away
To sell secondhand appliances at low prices
To teach a paid repair course
To collect donations for charity
quests.correctAnswer: To help neighbors fix items instead of throwing them away
quests.hint: The purpose is stated in the first sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says the café helps neighbors repair items for free instead of discarding them.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [A Museum's Interactive Exhibit] Rather than displaying artifacts behind glass, the museum's new exhibit allows visitors to handle replicas of ancient tools and try using them under a guide's supervision. Curators report that visitor surveys show significantly higher engagement and retention of historical information compared to the museum's traditional, hands-off exhibits.
quests.question: What do visitor surveys show about the new exhibit?
options: Lower interest than traditional exhibits
Higher engagement and retention of historical information
No noticeable difference from before
Concerns about the replicas' safety
quests.correctAnswer: Higher engagement and retention of historical information
quests.hint: The survey results are described in the last sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says surveys show significantly higher engagement and retention compared to traditional exhibits.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [A City's Noise Ordinance] After years of complaints from residents living near the entertainment district, the city council passed an ordinance limiting outdoor music volume after ten at night. Bar owners argued the rule would hurt business, but a compromise allowing indoor performances to continue as late as desired ultimately satisfied both sides.
quests.question: What compromise satisfied both residents and bar owners?
options: All outdoor music was banned permanently
Indoor performances could continue as late as desired
Bars were required to close earlier
Residents were offered financial compensation
quests.correctAnswer: Indoor performances could continue as late as desired
quests.hint: The compromise is described in the last sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says the compromise allowing indoor performances to continue late satisfied both sides.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [A Financial Literacy Course] When the local high school added a mandatory personal finance course, some parents worried it would take time away from traditional academic subjects. A year later, however, a survey of graduates found that most credited the course with helping them avoid common financial mistakes, such as high-interest debt, during their first year after graduation.
quests.question: What did most graduates say about the finance course, according to the survey?
options: It helped them avoid common financial mistakes
It should have replaced more subjects
It was less useful than expected
It made them avoid saving money
quests.correctAnswer: It helped them avoid common financial mistakes
quests.hint: The graduates' opinion is explained in the last sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says most graduates credited the course with helping them avoid financial mistakes like high-interest debt.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [An Urban Beekeeping Program] Rooftop beekeeping has become increasingly common in cities, with hotels and office buildings installing hives to support local pollinators and, in some cases, produce their own honey. Beekeepers note that urban bees are often surprisingly healthy, since cities typically use fewer pesticides than large agricultural farms.
quests.question: Why are urban bees often surprisingly healthy, according to beekeepers?
options: Cities have a warmer climate year-round
Urban hives are cleaned more often
Urban bees produce less honey
Cities typically use fewer pesticides than farms
quests.correctAnswer: Cities typically use fewer pesticides than farms
quests.hint: The explanation is given in the last sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says beekeepers attribute the bees' health to cities using fewer pesticides than agricultural farms.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [A Company's Return-to-Office Policy] After two years of fully remote work, the company announced employees would need to return to the office three days a week. Leadership argued the change would strengthen collaboration, though an internal survey conducted afterward revealed that many employees felt the decision undervalued the flexibility they had come to rely on.
quests.question: How did many employees feel about the return-to-office decision, according to the survey?
options: They felt fully supportive of the change
They were indifferent to the decision
They felt it undervalued the flexibility they relied on
They requested even more office days
quests.correctAnswer: They felt it undervalued the flexibility they relied on
quests.hint: The employees' reaction is described in the last sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says the survey revealed many employees felt the decision undervalued their flexibility.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [A Coral Restoration Project] Marine biologists have begun growing coral fragments in underwater nurseries before transplanting them onto damaged reefs, a technique that has shown promising early results in speeding up reef recovery. However, researchers caution that this approach only addresses part of the problem, since rising ocean temperatures remain the primary threat to coral survival long-term.
quests.question: What caution do researchers give about the coral nursery technique?
options: It has shown no positive results at all
It only addresses part of the problem
It is more expensive than natural recovery
It has been banned in most countries
quests.correctAnswer: It only addresses part of the problem
quests.hint: The researchers' caution appears in the last sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says researchers caution that the technique only addresses part of the problem, since rising temperatures remain the main threat.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [A Public Speaking Workshop] Many participants in the public speaking workshop initially assumed that eliminating filler words like 'um' was the key to sounding confident. Instructors instead focus on pacing and pausing, explaining that a well-placed silence often conveys more authority than rushing to fill every gap in speech.
quests.question: What do instructors focus on instead of eliminating filler words?
options: Memorizing entire speeches
Speaking as quickly as possible
Pacing and pausing
Using more formal vocabulary
quests.correctAnswer: Pacing and pausing
quests.hint: The instructors' actual focus is named in the second sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says instructors focus on pacing and pausing rather than simply removing filler words.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [A Rise in Bicycle Commuting] City data shows a steady increase in bicycle commuting over the past five years, a trend officials partly attribute to newly protected bike lanes that physically separate cyclists from car traffic. Commuters report feeling far safer on these routes than on the painted lanes used previously, which offered little real protection.
quests.question: Why do commuters report feeling safer on the new bike lanes?
options: The lanes are wider than car lanes
The lanes are monitored by cameras
The lanes physically separate cyclists from car traffic
The lanes are only used during the day
quests.correctAnswer: The lanes physically separate cyclists from car traffic
quests.hint: The reason for increased safety is explained in the first sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says the new lanes physically separate cyclists from traffic, unlike the previous painted lanes.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [A Company's Product Recall] After discovering a rare defect that could cause overheating in a small batch of laptops, the manufacturer issued a voluntary recall rather than waiting for regulators to require one. Industry analysts noted that acting quickly, even before any serious incidents occurred, likely helped protect the company's reputation more than a delayed response would have.
quests.question: What did industry analysts say about the company's quick action?
options: It was required by law
It caused the company to lose money
It was unnecessary since no harm occurred
It likely helped protect the company's reputation
quests.correctAnswer: It likely helped protect the company's reputation
quests.hint: The analysts' opinion is stated in the last sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says analysts believed acting quickly helped protect the company's reputation.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [A Shift in Grocery Shopping Habits] Surveys show that a growing number of shoppers now plan meals around what is on sale or in season, rather than choosing recipes first and then buying whatever ingredients they require. Nutritionists note this shift often leads to more varied diets, since shoppers end up trying vegetables they might not have otherwise picked.
quests.question: What effect do nutritionists say this shift in shopping habits often has?
options: It usually increases grocery spending
It reduces the amount of food bought
It discourages trying new vegetables
It often leads to more varied diets
quests.correctAnswer: It often leads to more varied diets
quests.hint: The nutritionists' observation is stated in the last sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says nutritionists note the shift often leads to more varied diets.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [A School's No-Homework Trial] One elementary school eliminated traditional homework for a semester, replacing it with a nightly requirement of twenty minutes of independent reading instead. Teachers reported no decline in test scores, and several noted that students seemed to arrive at school less stressed and more willing to participate in class discussions.
quests.question: What did several teachers notice about students during the trial?
options: They performed worse on tests
They seemed less stressed and more willing to participate
They read far less than before
They asked for traditional homework back
quests.correctAnswer: They seemed less stressed and more willing to participate
quests.hint: The teachers' observation is in the last sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says teachers noticed students seemed less stressed and more willing to participate in class.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [A Rise in Urban Foraging] Interest in urban foraging, or gathering wild edible plants within city limits, has grown alongside broader curiosity about sustainable food sources. Experts caution that foragers must be certain of a plant's identity before eating it, since several edible-looking wild plants have toxic look-alikes that can cause serious illness.
quests.question: What caution do experts give about urban foraging?
options: Foraging is illegal in most cities
Wild plants rarely taste good
Some edible-looking plants have toxic look-alikes
Foraged food is less nutritious than store food
quests.correctAnswer: Some edible-looking plants have toxic look-alikes
quests.hint: The experts' warning is explained in the last sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says experts warn that some edible-looking wild plants have toxic look-alikes.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [A Change in Airline Boarding Order] After analyzing years of boarding data, one airline switched from boarding by seat section to a system based on the number of carry-on bags passengers had, aiming to reduce the aisle congestion that typically slows the process down. Early results suggest average boarding times have dropped by nearly four minutes per flight.
quests.question: What was the airline trying to reduce by changing its boarding system?
options: The cost of checked baggage
Aisle congestion that slows the process down
The number of delayed flights
Complaints about seat assignments
quests.correctAnswer: Aisle congestion that slows the process down
quests.hint: The airline's goal is explained in the first sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says the airline aimed to reduce aisle congestion that typically slows down boarding.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [A Debate Over Standardized Testing] Critics of standardized testing argue that a single exam cannot fairly capture a student's full range of abilities, particularly for students who experience test anxiety or come from under-resourced schools. Supporters counter that, despite its flaws, standardized testing still provides one of the few consistent measures available for comparing students across vastly different schools and regions.
quests.question: What do supporters of standardized testing argue, according to the passage?
options: It fairly captures every student's full abilities
It should be replaced immediately
It eliminates the effects of test anxiety
It provides a consistent measure for comparing students across schools
quests.correctAnswer: It provides a consistent measure for comparing students across schools
quests.hint: The supporters' argument is in the second sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says supporters believe standardized testing offers a consistent way to compare students across different schools.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [A Rise in Repair Cafés and Right-to-Repair Laws] As electronics have become harder for consumers to fix themselves, several countries have introduced 'right-to-repair' laws requiring manufacturers to make spare parts and repair manuals available to the public. Supporters say the laws could significantly extend the lifespan of devices, reducing the volume of electronic waste sent to landfills each year.
quests.question: What do supporters believe the right-to-repair laws could achieve?
options: Extend the lifespan of devices and reduce electronic waste
Lower the price of all new electronics
Eliminate the need for manufacturers
Increase how often people buy new devices
quests.correctAnswer: Extend the lifespan of devices and reduce electronic waste
quests.hint: The claimed benefit is described in the last sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says supporters believe the laws could extend device lifespans and reduce electronic waste.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [A Look at Multigenerational Workplaces] As five different generations now work side by side for the first time in modern history, some companies have introduced reverse mentoring programs, pairing younger employees with senior leaders to share knowledge on new technology and workplace trends. Leaders who participate often say the experience challenges assumptions they did not realize they held.
quests.question: What do participating leaders often say about reverse mentoring?
options: It challenges assumptions they did not realize they held
It wastes time better spent on other tasks
It only benefits younger employees
It replaces the need for formal training
quests.correctAnswer: It challenges assumptions they did not realize they held
quests.hint: The leaders' reaction is described in the last sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says leaders often report that reverse mentoring challenges assumptions they were not aware of.
